thread.title: Stocks Give Up Opening Gains As Tesla Slides, Twitter Blasts Higher

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Give Up Opening Gains As Tesla Slides, Twitter Blasts Higher
text:
Stocks backed out of early mixed trade Thursday, with the Nasdaq following the Dow industrials and S&P 500 into moderate losses.
A two-year federal budget deal moving toward a possible vote Thursday had generated early optimism among investors, as earnings reports from Tesla ( TSLA ), Twitter ( TWTR ) others were factors in the morning's trade.
X The Nasdaq Composite popped 0.3% at the open, but quickly began trimming its gains. Viacom ( VIAB ) led the Nasdaq 100, up almost 11% after reporting its fiscal first-quarter results.
The   slipped 0.4% and the S&P 500 was down 0.2%. Verizon ( VZ ) and General Electric ( GE ) weighed on the Dow, down more than 1% each. HanesBrands ( HBI ) took the S&P 500's worst loss, falling more than 8% after its Q4 report.
The morning's leading economic release showed first-time unemployment claims declining to 221,000 in the week ended Feb. 3, according to the Labor Department. That was down from 230,000 applications in the prior week, and was far below economist consensus estimates for an increase to 235,000 claims.
Merck Leads Dow; Tesla Slumps, Canada Goose Dives; Twitter Takes Flight Declining issues led risers by more than 2-to-1 on the Dow just after the open. Merck ( MRK ) took an early lead, up 0.8%.
Apple ( AAPL ) inched up 0.1%, while the FANG stock tech leaders all lost ground. Shares continue to struggle to hold support at their 200-day moving average.
Chip stocks were under pressure just after the open, after taking some steep losses on Wednesday. But Nvidia ( NVDA ) managed a 1% gain in early trade, moving the stock beyond buy range above a 218.77 buy point at the open.
Tesla slipped 2.8% after reporting generally better-than-forecast fourth-quarter results after Wednesday's close. Tesla is technically in a consolidation with a handle buy point of 360.60, but its relative strength line is lagging, and the stock has had trouble gaining any altitude above its 10-week moving average.
Twitter spiked 20% after reporting fourth-quarter revenue and earnings growth above analysts' targets . The stock is extended after clearing a cup-with-handle base in December, and from a January rebound off 10-week support.
Fast-moving IPO Canada Goose Holdings ( GOOS ) faltered 15% following its fiscal third-quarter report. The apparel maker's earnings and revenue easily surpassed analyst projections , and the company announced that Chief Financial Officer John Black would be replaced later this year by Jonathan Sinclair, the CFO for shoe retailer Jimmy Choo. The loss sent Canada Goose shares to a test of support at their 10-week moving average, but the stock remains extended from a November breakout.
Most China-based stocks were quietly mixed, although online gaming leader NetEase ( NTES ) slumped 1.5% on a mixed fourth-quarter performance reported late Wednesday.
Dollar Rebounds, Oil Slips; Europe's Markets Trim Losses On BOE Rate Announcement The dollar bounced to its highest mark in two weeks, buoyed by optimism over a federal budget deal. Bonds reversed an early rebound, moving lower and lifting the 10-year yield by three basis points, to 2.87%.
Oil prices – a leading factor in Wednesday's high-volume selling — reversed course and edged higher, shaking off some of the pressure from data showing production levels of more than 10 million barrels per day in the U.S., reported by the Energy Information Administration on Wednesday.
Stocks in Europe fell hard in morning trade, but took back some ground after the Bank of England held interest rates steady, but hinted that an increase was in the works. The FTSE 100 in London dipped 0.9% and Frankfurt's DAX was down 1.2% in afternoon trade.
Asia's stock markets were mostly positive, with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 punching out a 1.1% advance. In China, Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rose 0.4%, while the Shanghai Composite dived 1.4%.
